speaker: provenzano
text: You council I have a proclamation here for Rett syndrome awareness month. Whereas Rett syndrome is a rare neurological condition that is rarely seen in males, but is seen almost exclusively in females. And is believed to occur in one in 10,000 female births. Parents believe they have a healthy child and symptoms do not appear until a regression between six to 18 months of age. And whereas throughout their lives, these courageous children will need total care and constant support from their family. They will combat many medical challenges. They may have seizures, osteoporosis, sclerosis, breath holding, hyperventilation, nutritional problems, and many more. Apraxia, which is the inability to motor plan is one of the most challenging aspects of Rett syndrome along with the loss of speech. Whereas in 1999, it was discovered that Rett syndrome is primarily caused by sporadic mutation in the MECP2 gene on the X chromosome. And since its discovery, there are many research projects taking place across Ontario and Canada. Whereas there's no Canadian Rett syndrome association, the Ontario Rett syndrome association has members from many provinces across Canada through donations and fundraising efforts. ORSA finances the Canadian Rett syndrome registry, has funded over 500,000 in Canadian Rett syndrome research projects. And financially supports the three Rett clinics in Ontario, with one in Ottawa, Toronto, and London. The Rett syndrome clinics provide direct critical support to the families and their child on care and management issues. And therefore I, Christian Provenzano, as mayor of the city of Sault Ste. Marie, do hereby proclaim October 2020 as Rett syndrome awareness month in Sault Ste. Marie. I urge all citizens to make an effort this month to learn more about Rett syndrome, fight stigma, fight Canada purple, and wear a purple ribbon to show support. Thank you.
